response.evidence: Among non-Hispanic Black or African American females in the dataset, there are 33 loan applications. Of these, 28 resulted in loans originated (84.8% approval rate) and 5 were denied (15.2% denial rate). The overall approval rate in the dataset is approximately 88.7%, meaning this demographic group's approval rate is only slightly lower. More specifically, examining the age range 35-44 (closest to the applicant's age of 35), there are 12 such applicants with 10 approvals (83.3% approval rate). The denials show varied financial profiles and are not concentrated in any specific characteristic pattern that would indicate discrimination. Similar approval rates are observed across other demographic groups with comparable financial profiles.

Analysis of 2378 loan applications shows 35-44 age group non-Hispanic Black/African American females had 11 applications with 9 approvals (81.8% approval rate). Overall approval rate was 88.6% (2107/2378). The small sample size and approval rate within normal variation range do not provide sufficient evidence of discrimination. Applications were denied across all demographic groups with similar debt-to-income ratios and loan-to-value ratios, suggesting decisions based on financial metrics rather than demographic characteristics.

Among 35-44 year-old non-Hispanic Black or African American females in the dataset, there are 16 total applications. Of these, 14 resulted in loan originations (87.5% approval rate) and only 2 were denied (12.5% denial rate). This approval rate is comparable to or higher than many other demographic groups with similar financial profiles in the data, suggesting no evidence of systematic discrimination against this applicant demographic in the loan approval process.
